principles.text: When the indices fade on a lower timeframe but the bigger-picture daily is bullish and individual names show relative strength by breaking out, that's a great time to pull the trigger long.

Key lesson: holding many full-size positions without selling enough into strength means giving back large profits when the inevitable pullback hits; sell more into strength to free buying power and mental capital, trusting you can buy back even if you exit a leader early.

In a straight-up, low-pullback market, progressive (gradual) exposure works worse than in a basing market; it's acceptable to be more aggressive — but cap it (e.g. 4-5 positions/day, not 8) and reduce risk per trade (~0.3R) to control drawdown.

Stock selection: prefer liquid names (>=500M daily dollar volume or >=10B market cap); the big multi-week/month winners are the liquid ones institutions buy, and liquidity lets you size up and avoids gap-down risk.

Use the weekly chart for context: a name that looks weak on the daily (below 9/15/21 EMA) can actually be pulling back into the weekly 9/21 EMA after a long base while building higher lows (e.g. NEP, IREN) — a setup to enter early before it's hard to chase.
Don't add to a winner: adding raises average cost and, with a 25-30% initial size, pushes the position to an unmanageable 40-50%; a stop-out on the add also hurts your mindset on the whole trade.
